$comment: Files a RUN generated that an update must preserve WHEN THEY ALREADY EXIST at $DEST — while still letting a fresh install (or a project a later ref newly adds) receive them for the first time. Same mechanism as operator-config-paths.json (snapshot, extract, restore), deliberately NOT run-state-paths.json's tar --exclude: every path below is TRACKED in git, so excluding it outright would leave a first install without it.
$why: Live 2026-09-05. A run reached pause 1 after 1h10m and $8.89 — a 49-agent roster, 41 provisioned prompts, the story assigned to a minted 'checkout-forms-engineer'. Updating that install in place with install.sh --dest replaced the mint's own outputs with whatever the ref's history held: the roster came back holding 'checkout-form-engineer' while the PRD still named the minted one, and the resume died with 'roster derivation FAILED — refusing to continue with agents that have no identity'. No copy of the minted profile survived anywhere on disk, so the entire mint was unrecoverable.
$boundary: run-state-paths.json already covers what LOOKS like evidence — logs, runs, spool, kb. These are evidence too: each is the product of a paid model call and cannot be reproduced without paying again. They are listed here rather than there because they are tracked and a first install needs them.
$promptCache: The cache is what makes a prompt generated ONCE per codeline instead of once per run. project-prompt-builder.js keys each entry by the template digest and, for prompts naming a minted role, the roster digest — so an unchanged prompt is reused. The mechanism worked; the update defeated it. .prompt-cache is TRACKED (78 files, 39 for metrolinx at v1.43), so every install.sh --dest --ref extracted the committed cache over the install's own. Those entries were generated against another run's roster, so no rolesDigest matched and all 39 regenerated. Measured 2026-09-05: prompt-builder $1.25/25 calls + prompt-review $1.51/16 calls = 36% of the run's spend, paid again on every republish. Operator: 'it does not have to be generated again and again ... I want it to be tagged to a codeline and reused for the codeline.'
$codelineNote: The cache is keyed BY CODELINE: entries live at .prompt-cache/<codeline>/<id>.json, so the nested pattern is what preserves them. The flat pattern above is kept because entries written before that change sit at the root until the first run declaring a codeline adopts them (project-prompt-builder.js migrateFlatEntries) — dropping it would discard them mid-migration.
$markerNote: The completion marker has NO .json extension — its NAME is the claim (.complete-<codeline>) — so the *.json pattern above does not match it. Without this line an update silently drops the marker and the next run re-mints and re-provisions everything, which is exactly the cost the cache exists to avoid.
